# Purpose and scope

Small virus retentive filtration is the dedicated virus removal step of the A-Mab drug
substance process, and this plan defines the studies that will characterize it. The step
removes virus by size, inside the structure of the membrane, and because it works on a
principle that has nothing in common with the low-pH hold at Step 6 or with the anion
exchange step at Step 8, its clearance is claimed as a separate module of the viral safety
argument [@ichq5a]. This plan states what will be studied, how the studies will be
executed and analysed, and the criteria against which the results will be judged. It is
written before any data exist and contains no findings.

The scope is the `{python} n_fac` operating parameters of the step, `{python} vol_name`
and `{python} pres_name`, studied together over the characterization ranges given in
@tbl-params. Both will be varied in a multivariate design on a qualified scale-down
spiking model, using the two model viruses that bound the retention challenge at this step
and are reported throughout this package: minute virus of mice (MVM) as the small
non-enveloped virus and xenotropic murine leukaemia virus (XMuLV) as the large enveloped
virus [@ichq5a]. Step yield will be measured at every design setting, on the unspiked
control run that accompanies each clearance run, so that any operating region proposed for
viral safety can also be checked against recovery.

Several things are outside this plan. The membrane itself is qualified by its
manufacturer, and this study does not repeat that qualification; it characterizes the
operating parameters the manufacturing site controls. The cumulative clearance claim for
the drug substance is assembled in PCMR-001 from this step and from Step 6 and Step 8, and
this plan covers only the contribution of Step 9. Product quality attributes are formed
upstream and are addressed in the documents for the steps that form and polish them.
The step does not by itself satisfy the cumulative clearance requirement for either model
virus, and no part of this study should be read as claiming that it does.

# Objectives

The study has five objectives.

- (i) Quantify the effect of `{python} vol_name` and `{python} pres_name` on MVM log
  reduction, on XMuLV log reduction and on step yield, across the characterization ranges
  in @tbl-params.
- (ii) Establish whether the two parameters interact, and whether either response is
  curved over the ranges studied, so that the operating region can be defined from a
  fitted model instead of from single-factor limits.
- (iii) Define the region of the two parameters over which the step meets its required
  log reduction for both model viruses.
- (iv) Derive a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each viral clearance
  attribute, and establish where the normal operating range sits in relation to it.
- (v) Classify each parameter under SOP-4001 and provide the ranges, controls and
  monitoring that the control strategy needs for Stage 2 [@fda2011].

These objectives are answered by the study reported in PCR-009. Nothing in this plan is
conditional on the outcome, and no objective may be dropped after the data are seen.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The step is operated in dead-end mode at constant pressure. The anion exchange pool is
passed through a pre-wetted small virus retentive filter, the filter is chased with buffer
to recover the product held up in the device, and the filter is integrity tested after use
(SOP-2012). The antibody passes through the retentive layer and virus particles are held
within it. Retention is a size effect, so the margin is widest for a large enveloped virus
and narrowest for a small non-enveloped one. MVM is the smallest of the model viruses used
for a monoclonal antibody process, and it therefore sets the retention challenge for this
step. XMuLV is much larger and is expected to be retained with a wide margin.

The step has been run on the Novacyte platform for three earlier antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab
and Z-Mab) with the same filter family, and because the mechanism of removal is a physical
one that does not depend on the product, the experience gained on those campaigns applies
directly to A-Mab [@amab2009]. No difference in performance is expected here. Platform
experience is the reason the study is small, and it is the expectation the study is
designed to confirm and bound. It is not a substitute for the study, because clearance may
be credited only from spiking data generated on the A-Mab process intermediate [@ichq5a].

Two mechanistic expectations shape the design. The first is that MVM log reduction falls
slowly as the volumetric load rises, because retentive capacity is consumed as the
membrane is loaded and the smallest particles are the first to find a path through. The
second is that pressure acts on flux and on the compaction of the retentive layer, so any
effect of pressure should be largest at high load, which makes it an interaction between
the two parameters and not a main effect of either. Both expectations are testable in the
design proposed in §6, and the study is arranged so that either can be refuted.

Step yield is expected to be high, and to be limited by the volume held up in the device
and not by anything that happens to the product. The step is not expected to change
any product quality attribute. Glycan, charge variant and aggregate attributes are formed
in the production bioreactor and are polished at the chromatography steps, and filtration
through a retentive membrane at moderate pressure has not induced aggregation or
fragmentation on the platform [@amab2009]. For this reason the study measures viral
clearance and yield, and carries no product quality design of its own.

## Quality attributes in scope

@tbl-cqa gives the two critical quality attributes this step contributes to. Both are
viral safety attributes, both are of very high criticality, and both are cumulative
process-level attributes: the acceptance criterion is a total log reduction across the
whole purification train, not a value that any one step delivers. Criticality is assigned
on the continuum used throughout the package, from the Tool #1 product of impact and
uncertainty, with high and very high treated as critical [@amab2009; @ichq9].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["lrv_mvm", "lrv_xmulv"]))
```

: Critical quality attributes to which this step contributes. {#tbl-cqa}

The register names the step at which each attribute is set. MVM clearance is assigned to
anion exchange and XMuLV clearance to low-pH inactivation, and this step contributes to
both. The division of credit matters most for MVM. A low-pH hold acts on the lipid
envelope, so it is credited with no clearance of a non-enveloped parvovirus, and the MVM
requirement of `{python} cum_mvm` log₁₀ rests on the anion exchange step (PCR-008) and on
this one, which is why the load limit set here is a viral safety control. XMuLV clearance
is shared across all three viral steps and its
cumulative requirement of `{python} cum_xmulv` log₁₀ is correspondingly higher. The
arithmetic that turns each cumulative requirement into a criterion for this step is given
in §7, and the consolidated claim is made in PCMR-001.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 assessed every parameter of this step before the characterization campaign began,
and its output is the study scope this plan executes. The assessment is summarized in
@tbl-risk.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(ra_scope(UO))
```

: Pre-characterization risk assessment for the step (RA-001). {#tbl-risk}

Both parameters carry the highest severity score available, because the attribute at risk
is viral safety and a failure of retention would not be corrected anywhere downstream.
Detection scores poorly at both parameters, because virus titre in the filtrate can be
measured only in a deliberately spiked study and never on a manufacturing batch, so the
process itself gives no direct in-process signal that retention has been lost. The
integrity test detects a damaged device, which is a different failure. Both parameters were
carried into the multivariate design by the risk ranking and filtering in RA-001, because
the effect of each is expected to depend on the other, and both were ranked at high
priority on severity.

RA-001 also fixed the ranges, and the reasoning is different for the two parameters.
`{python} vol_name` is studied to `{python} vol_hi` `{python} vol_unit`, well above the
upper edge of its normal operating range at `{python} vol_nor_hi` `{python} vol_unit`,
because the platform expectation is a slow decline in MVM clearance with load. A study
confined to the normal range would confirm that the step works and would say nothing about
where it stops working. `{python} pres_name` is studied over `{python} pres_rng`
`{python} pres_unit`, which brackets its normal operating range of `{python} pres_nor`
`{python} pres_unit` on both sides. The low edge is included because a long, slow
filtration is a distinct operating state and not merely a milder version of the target,
and the high edge because pressure is the parameter most likely to interact with load.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The clearance claim rests entirely on a scale-down model, because virus cannot be
introduced into a manufacturing batch. Viral safety guidance ICH Q5A requires the
small-scale system to be representative of the commercial step before clearance is credited
to it [@ichq5a], and SOP-1001 defines how that is demonstrated for this package. The model
is a small-area
device of the same membrane chemistry, the same retentive structure and the same housing
geometry as the commercial filter, operated at the same volumetric load per unit area and
the same pressure as the commercial step.

Qualification will compare the small-scale system against commercial-scale data on three
points: the flux profile through the load, product recovery, and the quality of the
filtrate. The comparison is made at the target operating point, with all parameters at
their set-points, since the purpose is to establish that the two scales behave alike when
the process is run as intended. Qualification is a prerequisite for the characterization
runs. No DoE run will be executed until the scale-down model report has been approved, and
a model that fails any of the three comparisons will be modified and requalified before
the study starts.

The warrant the model provides is specific. It supports claims about how the retention of
this membrane responds to volumetric load and pressure, because those are the variables
the model reproduces, and it does not support claims about the pooling, hold and transfer
operations that surround the step at commercial scale and are controlled by batch record.
Both bounds are carried through to the conclusions of PCR-009.

Replicated centre points are built into both designs, `{python} cp_scr` in the screening
design and `{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design. The variation among them is
the pure-error term against which lack of fit is judged (§5.5), and it is also the direct
measure of how reproducibly the scale-down model performs at one setting.

## Operation

The load material is the anion exchange pool. Its attributes are controlled to the
in-process criteria for that step (PCP-008) and are not varied in this study, so they are
identity- and quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized ones. The pool is
filtered to the target volumetric load at constant pressure, chased with the same buffer
to recover held-up product, and the device is integrity tested after use (SOP-2012).

For the clearance runs the load is spiked with a virus stock and then passed through a
pre-filter before the retentive filter. Pre-filtration removes virus aggregates, which
would otherwise be retained for reasons of size that have nothing to do with the
performance of the membrane and would inflate the log reduction. Every other condition is
held at platform values, so that the only deliberate differences between runs are the
factor settings listed in @tbl-appa and @tbl-appb.

## Analytical methods

Two validated infectivity assays carry the study. MVM titre is measured by TCID50 with
qPCR confirmation (AMV-3018) and XMuLV titre by TCID50 (AMV-3017). The log reduction
factor for each run is the difference between the titre of the spiked load and the titre
of the pooled filtrate, corrected for volume. @tbl-methods gives the validated performance
of both methods.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(method_perf_for(VIRUS_FILT_AMV_REFS, precision_with_unit=True))
```

: Validated performance of the analytical methods used for the study. {#tbl-methods}

Both assays report a titre on a log scale, so their intermediate precision is stated as a
log₁₀ standard deviation and not as a relative standard deviation. The MVM assay carries
an intermediate precision of `{python} mvm_prec` and the XMuLV assay `{python} xmulv_prec`.
Assay variation propagates into every log reduction factor, so the standard error of an
effect follows from it together with the replicated centre points of the design in which
the effect is estimated (§5.5). An effect of the order of the assay precision will not be
resolved by the screening design, and PCR-009 will report every effect with its standard
error and its p-value and not as a bare magnitude.

The limit of quantitation sets a second and less obvious bound. When no virus is detected
in the filtrate the log reduction cannot be reported as a number, and it is instead
reported as at least the difference between the load titre and the limit of quantitation of
the assay, which for the MVM method is a filtrate titre of `{python} mvm_loq`. Such a
result is censored, not measured, and a
censored value cannot be
treated as an observation in a regression without biasing the fit. Runs that give a
censored result will be identified in PCR-009 and the model for that response will be
fitted to the runs that are not censored, with the censored runs reported alongside.

Step yield is not a virological measurement. It is calculated by mass balance across the
step, from the protein mass in the load and the protein mass in the pooled filtrate, using
the concentration method that supports the formulation step (AMV-3019, listed in PCP-010).
The full validation data for all three methods are held in their validation reports and are
not reproduced here.

## Sampling plan

Each run generates four kinds of sample. The load is sampled before spiking, to establish
the starting material, and after spiking, to establish the input titre. The filtrate is
collected in sequence as successive fractions across the load, so that clearance can be
followed as a function of the volume already filtered. The fractions are pooled to give the
cumulative filtrate, which is the sample the log reduction factor is calculated from. The
post-use integrity test result is recorded for every run.

Fractionation is included so that clearance can be followed through the load. Breakthrough
is a phenomenon of the later part of the load, and a single pooled sample averages the last
fraction together with the first and hides it. The fractions cost assay capacity and
nothing else, and they are what allows the study to locate where in the load a decline in
clearance begins.

Centre-point runs are replicated: `{python} cp_scr` replicates in the screening design and
`{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design. Two controls accompany every clearance
run. An unspiked run establishes yield and integrity without virus present, and a spike
hold control establishes that the virus stock is stable over the duration of the run, so
that a loss of titre is not mistaken for retention.

## Statistical methods

The analysis follows SOP-1002. Both factors are analysed in coded units, with the low and
high edges of the characterization range coded −1 and +1 and the centre of the design coded
0. Coding puts the two parameters on one scale, so that effects can be compared directly
and the fitted coefficients read as the change in the response over half the range studied.

The screening design is analysed by ordinary least squares with both main effects and their
interaction. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in
the response from the low edge of a factor to the high edge. The response-surface data are
analysed with the full quadratic model, which adds a squared term for each factor to the
main effects and the interaction. Significance is judged at α = `{python} ALPHA`
throughout.

Model adequacy will be assessed on four things, and all four are reported in PCR-009: the
coefficient of determination and its adjusted form, the predicted coefficient of
determination from the PRESS statistic, the overall model F test, and an analysis of
variance that partitions the residual into lack of fit and pure error. Pure error comes
from the replicated centre points, which is why they are in both designs. A model with
significant lack of fit describes the data it was fitted to but does not predict, and a
model that fails this test will not be used to define an operating region.

The screening design and the response-surface design do different jobs, and this plan keeps
them separate. The screening design identifies which factors are active and whether they
interact. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and it alone is the basis of
the design space and of the proven acceptable ranges in §8. Effect estimates from the
screening runs will be reported as evidence of which factors matter, and will not be
presented as predictions.

A factor with no significant effect on a response is a result and will be reported as one.
It is evidence that the response is robust to that factor over the range studied, it is
retained in the knowledge space on that basis, and it is classified accordingly under
SOP-4001.

Commercial-scale capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} n_mc` batches of the whole purification train, with every parameter varying about
its set-point across its normal operating range. It is reported for each viral clearance
attribute as a one-sided capability index against the cumulative drug substance
requirement, together with the margin between the simulated mean and that requirement. The
index is a property of the train and not of this step alone, and the contribution this step
makes to it is the log reduction reported against the criteria of §7. This plan sets
no numeric acceptance threshold for the capability index, because none is established for
the campaign; capability is reported as a measure of margin and is interpreted against the
criticality of the attribute [@amab2009].

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

@tbl-params gives the parameters, their set-points, the ranges to be studied and the normal
operating ranges. @tbl-legend gives the letter codes used for the factors in the design
matrices and in the effect tables of PCR-009.


```{python}
#| output: asis

```

: Factor legend for the design matrices. {#tbl-legend}

Both parameters are assigned to the multivariate design, and each characterization range
contains its normal operating range and extends well above it. `{python} vol_name` runs
from `{python} vol_rng` `{python} vol_unit` against a normal range of `{python} vol_nor`
`{python} vol_unit`, so the two share their lower edge at `{python} vol_nor_lo`
`{python} vol_unit` and the studied range extends above the normal one to
`{python} vol_hi` `{python} vol_unit`.
`{python} pres_name` runs from `{python} pres_rng` `{python} pres_unit` against a normal
range of `{python} pres_nor` `{python} pres_unit`, which it brackets on both sides. The
studied range is the knowledge space for this step. The design space will be a region
inside it, and the normal operating range will lie within that region, touching the studied
range only at the lower load edge.

The centre of the design is not the set-point of the process. It sits at
`{python} vol_centre`
`{python} vol_unit` and `{python} pres_centre` `{python} pres_unit`, above the set-points
of `{python} vol_sp` `{python} vol_unit` and `{python} pres_sp` `{python} pres_unit`,
because coding places the centre at the midpoint of each characterization range and both
ranges extend further above the target than below it. Both centre settings lie inside the
normal operating ranges of @tbl-params, so the centre point is a condition the process is
licensed to run at and not a worst case. The worst case for this step is defined in §7, and
it is a corner of the design and not its centre.

## Screening design

The screening study is a full factorial in the `{python} n_fac` factors at two levels,
augmented with `{python} cp_scr` replicated centre points, giving `{python} n_scr` runs
(@tbl-appa). The design is not saturated. It estimates both main effects and their
interaction independently, and the replicated centre points add an estimate of pure error
and a test for curvature.

The purpose of this stage is to identify which of the two parameters drives each response,
and whether the interaction expected in §4.1 is present. The screening fit will not be used
to predict a response at an untested setting. Where curvature is detected at the centre
points, the two-level design cannot describe it, and the response-surface stage exists for
that reason.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design in the same
`{python} n_fac` factors, with `{python} n_runs` runs across the two stages and
`{python} n_rsm` runs in this one (@tbl-appb). It comprises the `{python} n_corner`
factorial corners, `{python} n_axial` axial runs placed at the face centres of the design
region, and `{python} cp_rsm` replicated centre points. The axial runs sit on the faces and
not outside them, so that no run falls outside the characterization ranges given in
@tbl-params.

This design supports the full quadratic model in both factors. It is the model from which
the operating region and the proven acceptable ranges are derived, and it is the only model
in this plan that is used to predict a response of this step. Its predictions are bounded
by the ranges in @tbl-params, by the qualified scale-down model described in §5.1, and by
the load material specification of the anion exchange step.

## Univariate assessment

No parameter of this step is assigned to a univariate study. RA-001 assigned both
parameters to the multivariate design (@tbl-risk), and with only `{python} n_fac` factors
in the design there is no case for separating them. The interaction is one of the things
the study exists to test.

Three further inputs are known to affect virus filtration in general and are nonetheless
not studied here. Buffer pH, conductivity and protein concentration have been shown across
the platform to have little or no effect on the retention of either model virus over the
ranges the process visits [@amab2009], and the anion exchange step delivers a pool whose
composition is controlled to a narrow specification (PCP-008). These inputs are therefore
carried as controlled conditions and not as factors, and the justification for that is
prior knowledge and not a study performed here.

The post-use filter integrity test is a procedural control and not a parameter. It is
executed on every run of this study and on every commercial batch, and its result is
recorded as an attribute of the run. A failed integrity test invalidates the clearance
result of that run.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

This section states the criteria before the data exist. @tbl-acceptance gives what each
measured response must achieve, and the basis of each criterion.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.acceptance_table(UO))
```

: Acceptance criteria for the measured responses. {#tbl-acceptance}

The two viral clearance criteria are step contributions and are derived, not specified. The
drug substance requirement is cumulative, and the requirement placed on this step is that
requirement less the clearance credited to the other steps of the train. On that basis this
step must deliver at least `{python} acc_mvm` log₁₀ of MVM clearance and at least
`{python} acc_xmulv` log₁₀ of XMuLV clearance. Neither figure is a specification in its own
right. Both move if the clearance credited to Step 6 or Step 8 changes, and PCR-009 will
state the values in force when the study reports. Step yield has no criterion of this kind.
It is a process performance attribute, it is reported for every run, and it is used to
check that an operating region proposed on viral safety grounds is also a region the
process can be run in.

The study is judged on four decisions, each of them made against evidence stated in
PCR-009.

- (i) The scale-down model is qualified. Flux profile, recovery and filtrate quality at the
  target operating point are comparable with commercial-scale data under SOP-1001. This
  decision is made before the characterization runs, and a failure stops the study.
- (ii) Each response-surface model is adequate. The overall model is significant at
  α = `{python} ALPHA`, lack of fit is not significant against pure error, and the
  predicted coefficient of determination supports use of the model outside the runs it was
  fitted to. A response whose model fails these tests is reported from the observed data
  only, and no region is claimed from it.
- (iii) An operating region is defined. The fitted model predicts at least
  `{python} acc_mvm` log₁₀ for MVM and at least `{python} acc_xmulv` log₁₀ for XMuLV
  everywhere in the proposed region, including at its worst-case corner. For this step the
  worst-case corner is the high edge of `{python} vol_name` taken together with the
  pressure edge that the fitted model shows to be less favourable, and the region is not
  accepted on the strength of its centre.
- (iv) Each parameter is classified. Classification follows SOP-4001 from the demonstrated
  effect on a critical quality attribute and from the risk of leaving the design space in
  routine operation. A parameter with a demonstrated effect that is nonetheless easy to
  control and far from the region boundary is a well-controlled critical process parameter;
  one that is hard to control, or whose boundary is close to the normal operating range, is
  a critical process parameter.

These criteria apply within the characterization ranges of @tbl-params and to material
produced on the qualified scale-down model. A result outside those ranges is outside this
plan. Any deviation from the plan will be recorded, investigated and impact assessed before
the affected data are used, and the disposition will be reported in PCR-009.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

A proven acceptable range is a range of one parameter over which a quality attribute stays
within acceptance, supported by data [@ichq8]. The design space this study will define is
multivariate, and the proven acceptable ranges complement it by stating, parameter by
parameter, how far each one may move on its own. Both are reported in PCR-009. This section
states how the ranges will be derived.

The acceptance basis is the one given in §7. For each viral clearance attribute the
criterion is the step contribution back-calculated from the cumulative requirement, which
is `{python} acc_mvm` log₁₀ for MVM and `{python} acc_xmulv` log₁₀ for XMuLV. Step yield
carries no such criterion and no proven acceptable range is derived for it.

Two analyses will be run for each combination of parameter and attribute. The first holds
the other parameter at its set-point and evaluates the fitted response-surface model across
the characterization range of the parameter of interest. The second propagates the normal
operating range of the other parameter by Monte-Carlo, drawing `{python} par_draws` values
at each of `{python} par_grid` points across the characterization range and taking the
two-sided 95% predictive interval of the fitted model at each point. The first analysis
answers what the parameter does when the rest of the process is at target. The second
answers what it does when the rest of the process is anywhere in its normal range, which is
the question a manufacturing site actually faces.

The decision rule is the same for both analyses. The proven acceptable range is the
contiguous interval of the parameter, containing its set-point, over which the attribute
stays within acceptance under that analysis. Under the first analysis the criterion is
applied to the predicted mean. Under the second it is applied to the predictive interval,
so the second range is the more demanding of the two and is expected to be the narrower.
Where the range covers the whole characterization range, PCR-009 will say so and will state
that the parameter was not limiting over the region studied. Where it is narrower, PCR-009
will name the attribute that binds it and the margin remaining between the range and the
normal operating range.

Each proven acceptable range will be reported with a plot of the parameter against the
attribute, with the acceptance limit drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the
set-point and normal operating range marked. The at set-point and the NOR-propagated
analyses appear as the two panels of that plot.

These ranges and the design space answer different questions, and the difference matters
when the results are read. A proven acceptable range is univariate, in that it moves one
parameter and holds or averages the other. The design space is the multivariate region in
which both parameters may move together. When both proven acceptable ranges span their
whole characterization ranges, the binding constraint on the operating region is the
worst-case corner of the multivariate region and no univariate range at all, and PCR-009
will present it that way. All of these ranges are bounded by the characterization ranges of
@tbl-params, by the fitted model, and by the scale-down model on which the data were
generated.

# Data management and integrity

All raw data, calculations and reported results are governed by the ALCOA+ principles.
Assay data are captured in the validated laboratory systems of the testing laboratory,
process data are recorded on the executed run records for each scale-down run, and both are
attributable to the analyst or operator who generated them.

The statistical analysis is performed with the seeded, version-controlled analysis code
described in SOP-1002, so the tables and figures of PCR-009 can be regenerated from the raw
data without manual steps. A second qualified person reviews the analysis against the raw
data before the report is issued.

Changes to data after entry are made as tracked corrections with a reason recorded. No
result is excluded from the analysis without a documented technical justification, and any
exclusion is reported in PCR-009 together with its effect on the fitted model.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-009, the characterization report for the step. It
reports the executed design, the fitted models, the operating region, the proven acceptable
ranges, the capability estimate, the parameter classifications and any deviations from this
plan. PCR-009 rolls up into PCMR-001, which consolidates the clearance claim across the
three viral steps.

The work is sequenced in four phases. The scale-down model is qualified and its report
approved. The screening design is then executed and analysed. The response-surface design
follows, and is executed on the same model with the same load material specification.
Analysis, capability estimation and reporting complete the sequence. No calendar dates are
committed in this synthetic document. The sequence is what the plan commits to.

# Risks and assumptions

Four risks could affect the study, and each has a defined response.

The scale-down model may not represent the commercial step across the whole range studied,
even if it does so at the target operating point where it is qualified. This is the
weightiest of the four, because every conclusion of the study inherits it. It is managed by
qualifying against commercial data at the target point, by holding the model construction
identical to the commercial device, and by stating the limitation in the conclusions of
PCR-009 rather than leaving it to be inferred.

The virus stock may contain aggregates, which are retained by size and inflate the log
reduction. Pre-filtration of the spiked load is the standard control and is built into the
method (§5.2).

Clearance may exceed what the assay can measure, particularly for XMuLV, which prior
knowledge suggests will be retained with a wide margin. The result is then censored at the
limit of quantitation and the model for that response is weaker than the model for MVM.
This is a known and accepted outcome; it is handled as described in §5.3, and it does not
affect the MVM analysis, which is the analysis that governs the load limit.

Filter-to-filter and lot-to-lot variation in the membrane is not a factor in this design.
Devices from more than one lot will be used across the runs where supply allows, and any
run-order or lot effect will be examined in the residuals of the fitted models.

Three assumptions are made and are recorded here so they can be challenged. Platform
experience with the same filter family on three earlier antibodies transfers to A-Mab,
because the mechanism of removal is a physical one and does not depend on the product. The
anion exchange pool used in the study is representative of the commercial load. The
clearance credited to Step 6 and Step 8 stands as reported in PCR-006 and PCR-008, since
the criteria in §7 are derived from it.
